        </div>
        <div class="articles-list">
          <div class="article-category">
        <div class="u-mb-4">
          <!-- MyoSim logo removed to prevent GitHub authentication prompts on mobile -->
          <p class="page-lede">
            MyoSim is an open-source software library for simulating muscle-driven movement, providing tools 
            for biomechanical modeling and analysis. MyoSim enables researchers to build and simulate 
            models of muscle-tendon systems, analyze muscle activation patterns, and study the dynamics 
            of movement. The software is particularly useful for understanding how muscles generate forces 
            and how these forces produce movement in biomechanical systems, including golf swing analysis.
          </p>
          <div class="site-card site-card--callout u-mb-4">
            <h2 class="u-mb-1">Authority Boundary</h2>
            <p>
              <strong>This establishes</strong> educational overviews of muscle-driven simulation concepts, Hill-type muscle-tendon dynamics, and open-source library links.
              Current UpstreamDrift software engine support tiers (MyoSuite is experimental stack) are governed separately on the <a href="programming/engines.html">Engines and Runtime Support</a> catalog.
            </p>
            <p>
              <strong>This does not establish</strong> verified in-vivo muscle force reproduction, cross-subject activation optimality, or clinical validity for rehabilitation or sports performance.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

          <div id="available-models" class="category-section">
            <h2 class="category-title">Available Models</h2>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Muscle-Tendon Unit Models</h3>
          <p>Models of individual muscle-tendon units with detailed force-length-velocity relationships, 
          enabling analysis of muscle force production and energy consumption during movement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Multi-Muscle System Models</h3>
          <p>Models of systems with multiple muscles acting on joints, allowing for analysis of 
          muscle coordination, synergies, and force sharing in complex movements like the golf swing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Forward Dynamics Simulations</h3>
          <p>Forward dynamics models that simulate movement from muscle activations, enabling predictive 
          analysis and optimization of movement patterns and muscle activation strategies.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Muscle Activation Models</h3>
          <p>Models for simulating muscle activation dynamics, including excitation-activation coupling, 
          allowing for realistic simulation of muscle behavior in response to neural commands.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
